added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own two gate arms as the manifest records them: baseline_suite at 2fdaf318e ran `uv run pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/standard_names/test_docs_locus_definition.py` to 1 failure (tests/standard_names/test_docs_locus_definition.py::test_two_subjects_render_the_identical_locus_sentence, a stale assertion the node was briefed to repair) and after_suite at d0e1b7b5a ran the same file plus tests/standard_names/test_docs_prompt_locus.py to 0 failures, so the after arm introduces no new failure id and the one delta is the removed stale failure. I re-read both log_path files and they carry those summaries and their EXIT= lines.

findings.text: blocking: blocking: the generate-path docs writer is still told to paraphrase the locus. generate_docs_system.md:426 renders, under the same locus_context that workers.py:9889-9904 passes to both halves of the generate request, "Locus gloss (for accurate prose - do NOT quote verbatim): {{ locus_context.description }}", the identical invitation the brief had removed from refine_docs_user.md. The node goal is "Make the docs writer name the locus without defining it", so the goal is unmet on the path that writes documentation, and the landing fragment claim at shc-writer-no-locus-restatement.html:21 that the gloss instruction is removed is true of one prompt only. That prompt file is outside the node write scope, so the repair needs a scope extension rather than an in-node fix.

follow-on: follow-on: test_generate_docs_prompt_names_locus_without_defining_it renders sn/generate_docs_user only, so its do-NOT-quote-verbatim assertion cannot redden on the surviving gloss in generate_docs_system.md:426; the declared control negctl-prompt.log restored the gloss in refine_docs_user.md and failed only test_refine_docs_prompt_names_locus_without_defining_it (1 failed / 1 passed), leaving the generate arm uncontrolled. Rendering sn/generate_docs_system in the same test would make the guard cover the path production actually sends (workers.py:9904).

follow-on: follow-on: test_prepositional_locus_mention_is_not_a_definition asserts a not-in for a sentence the base pattern matches and the untouched preposition exemption at docs_gates.py:688-704 already lets through, so it is green at 2fdaf318e as well as at head and cannot fail when this node change is reverted; measured directly, the base quantifier {0,2} matches "the plasma boundary is" in the xenon sentence and the exemption suppresses it. The done-when clause that each new gate test fails with its change reverted is therefore met for one of the two, and this assertion is a forward guard on the exemption rather than a control for this change.

follow-on: follow-on: the landing fragment states at lines 17-23 that the gloss instruction is removed and that both docs prompts now state the no-restatement rule, but three prompts render locus_context in production (workers.py:9894, 9904, 11100) and generate_docs_system.md:426 was left carrying the gloss, so the record overstates the landed effect a reader would take from it.
